themes.name: AI compute: NVIDIA's supply chain
themes.what: Dell reported record quarterly revenue of $54.9 billion, up 103%, with AI server revenue of $22.0 billion and a record $132.3 billion AI backlog, and raised its AI server outlook to $78 billion (Dell). The stock still fell: DELL closed 297.06 Nov 25 after an 11.8% drop Tuesday (Massive). HPE guided its AI unit's margin down to about 14%. On Nov 25 S&P Global put Nvidia's AA rating on CreditWatch negative over management and governance risk (S&P Global; CNBC).
themes.for_you: Demand is not the problem; the price paid for it is. Server makers book record orders at thinner margins, and memory makers like MU take the money. No chip or server entries: NVDA is 149.30, under its falling 200 day (202.62). MU fell 15% in two days, so no puts on it either.

themes.name: Healthcare and Medtech: Aging, Heart, Sugar, Hearing, Sight
themes.what: Medtronic's fiscal Q2 cardiac ablation sales grew 58%, with 80% US growth, and organic revenue grew 6.5% (Medtronic 8-K). MDT fell 4.6% to 96.13 on Nov 24 and held at 96.06 on Nov 25 (Massive). On Nov 25 the USTR's China and India tariff reports named medical devices as targeted sectors (USTR).
themes.for_you: MDT is on the long term scan buy list at 96.06, inside its 84.54 to 97.64 zone and at its 94.80 long term point. It also sits 2.0% over its range low (94.13): a close under that on 1.5x volume would block puts. Buy in small pieces only if it holds 94.13.

countries.name: China
countries.what: The USTR proposed tariffs of up to 20% on Chinese goods not on its annex lists and up to 10% on Annex A goods, with Annex B goods exempt, under a Section 301 finding on excess factory capacity (USTR). The report names autos, batteries, chips, medical devices, robotics, solar and steel, among others. FXI fell 0.4% to 31.30 and BABA rose 1.7% on Nov 25 (Massive).
countries.for_you: No action. PDD sells Chinese goods into the US through Temu, so it is the most exposed. It has no buy point (under its falling 200 day). Nothing takes effect before the Jan 25 hearings; the China metals pause still runs to about Jan 27.

countries.name: European Union
countries.what: The USTR proposed a 15% tariff on all EU goods and up to 15% on Swiss goods, net of normal duties and existing Section 301 tariffs. The EU report names autos, chemicals and pharmaceuticals (USTR). US listed European names held up on Nov 25: SNY +4.8% to 54.39 (still rising on the Insmed deal), NVO +1.6%, STLA +6.4% (Massive).
countries.for_you: No action. European drug makers are named, but they already make many US drugs in the US, and the proposal can still change at the Jan 25 hearings. STLA is the most exposed: a carmaker shipping from Europe.

countries.name: India
countries.what: The US Trade Representative proposed tariffs of up to 25% on all Indian goods on Nov 25, or 17% if India reaches a trade deal, after finding India's industrial policies unfair under Section 301. The India report names health (pharmaceuticals and medical devices), steel, solar and tech hardware (USTR). Indian ADRs rose anyway on Nov 25: RDY +1.2% to 15.35, HDB +2.9%, INFY +4.2% (Massive). These are proposals: written comments are due Jan 5, 2027 and hearings start Jan 25, 2027 (USTR), so nothing takes effect before late January.
countries.for_you: RDY is the most exposed name on the dashboard: a generic drug maker that ships from India to the US. Its Nov 25 close over the pivot came on 4,289,544 shares, a hair under the 4,298,000 needed, so it is not confirmed either way. No new RDY swing until the tariff path is clearer. Services exporters like INFY are not tariffed goods, so they are left out of both lists.

countries.name: Japan
countries.what: The USTR proposed tariffs of up to 15% on all Japanese goods, net of normal duties and existing Section 301 tariffs, naming autos, steel, chips and optical fiber (USTR). The Nikkei fell 2.88% on Nov 25 (CNBC), but US listed Japanese names closed higher: TM +2.8% to 215.79, HMC +1.8% to 33.66, SONY +2.5% to 28.49 (Massive).
countries.for_you: SONY closed over its 28.30 breakout level on 1.67x volume on Nov 25 (dashboard buy point), the same day the tariff was proposed. Treat it as a watch, not an entry, until the half day Friday and next week show it holds. Autos carry the most risk: no puts on TM or HMC before the Jan 25 hearings.

countries.name: Mexico
countries.what: The USTR proposed new tariffs on 14 economies on Nov 25 but made no determination on Mexico or Norway, which were also investigated (USTR). Mexican ADRs rose: EWW +2.0% to 73.34, CX +3.8% to 9.89, FMX +2.0% to 127.92 (Massive).
countries.for_you: Mexico gains if factories move away from the 14 named economies. FMX has a range break down watch at 121.84 (ranges.json); it moved away from it. No action until a buy point forms.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.what: The USTR proposed tariffs of up to 15% on all Korean goods, net of normal duties, and said the plan accounts for the Korea Strategic Trade and Investment Deal (USTR). The KOSPI fell more than 6% on Nov 25 (CNBC); EWY fell 1.2% to 129.19 in New York (Massive).
countries.for_you: No action. EWY is in a confirmed break down after the Nov 5 selloff (ranges.json). No puts on Korean names.

countries.name: Taiwan
countries.what: The USTR proposed tariffs of up to 15% on all goods of Taiwan, net of normal duties, and said it accounts for the US and Taiwan reciprocal trade agreement. The report names electronics, semiconductors and telecom (USTR). TSM fell 2.0% to 342.34 and EWT 1.3% to 83.48 on Nov 25 (Massive).
countries.for_you: No chip entries. TSM fell for a second day after Monday's 14% jump. Wait for the AI group to stop making lower lows.
